failed_conditions.quote: Intra-process communication is disabled, consider enabling it by adding:  extra_arguments=[{'use_intra_process_comms' : True}] to the Servo composable node in the launch file

notes: Independently verified: issue #2632 quotes the warning advice verbatim and the resulting refusal ("Following advice of the warning leads to an error."). servo_node.cpp at tag 2.8.0 contains the warning at lines 72-76 and creates publishers with rclcpp::SystemDefaultsQoS() (lines 107, 112, 117, 123, 128, 132 — including node_->create_publisher<moveit_msgs::msg::ServoStatus>(servo_params_.status_topic, rclcpp::SystemDefaultsQoS()); exactly as the spec's evidence quotes). rclcpp publisher.hpp at 24.0.0 contains the throw statement verbatim at lines 170-173 (fetched from the tag). PR #2752's diff removes exactly the warning block and nothing else in that hunk. Eligibility: the refused value (keep-last depth-0 QoS profile on the intra-process path) crosses the moveit_servo -> rclcpp API boundary; the resolving change is deleting the misleading advice in consumer code, not a deployment name binding, build change, or firmware fault — stop_step 6 library API is right. Class `other` is right: the refused attribute is QoS history kind/depth, and the listed QoS classes cover only reliability/durability/deadline. The spec transparently marks the implicated entity as inferred from code (the subscription path throws a differently worded message) — sound. Loudness loud_documented/activate is right: a runtime-enforced refusal at component construction reported by the component container (S1 counts refusals the runtime enforced as loud). Resolution none is right: PR #2752 does not change the QoS passed to rclcpp, so the failed composition (Servo with intra-process enabled) still fails at the resolved revision; the only practical remedy is not enabling it, which is not a resolving change of the failed composition.
